summary: Syntax and imports are fine, and the program runs with a direct main() call. However, there are major implementation mismatches with the specified task: epidemic dynamics are not modeled (no transmission, Rt, or cases), several required entities and metrics are missing or only loosely approximated, and parameter names from the spec are not correctly mapped (e.g., simulation_duration_days, initial_mask_adoption_rate, rewiring_rate). Some logic/metric gaps exist (e.g., masks_purchased, stockout_events, subgroup_adoption_gap).

issues.description: No epidemic transmission dynamics are implemented: infection risk at locations, incident cases, Rt, peak incidence, and cumulative infections averted are not computed.
issues.solution: Implement an epidemic module (e.g., SEIR/SIR) coupled to location visits and mask usage to produce incident_cases, Rt, peak_incidence, and cumulative_infections_averted. Integrate mask efficacy parameters when computing transmission probabilities.

issues.description: Parameter names from the provided spec are not correctly mapped. Keys like simulation_duration_days, initial_mask_adoption_rate, and rewiring_rate are ignored or not used as intended.
issues.location: main() steps selection; SocialSimulation._extract_parameters(); SocialSimulation.initialize() uses initial_adoption_rate and simulation_days
issues.solution: Map spec parameters to internal names: use parameters.simulation_duration_days for steps; parameters.initial_mask_adoption_rate -> initial_adoption_rate; parameters.rewiring_rate -> rewire_prob; and generally read from data['parameters'] with correct keys.

issues.description: Required entities and interactions are simplified or missing: no Household, no Retailer class instances (single global SupplyChain instead), no explicit SocialNetwork class with rewiring behavior exposed.
issues.solution: Add Household, Retailer, and SocialNetwork classes per spec. Model households for norms/resource sharing; multiple retailers with stock levels/restock/pricing; a SocialNetwork entity with rewiring behavior and influence propagation.

issues.description: Several required metrics are missing or not computed accurately: masks_purchased, stockout_events, subgroup_adoption_gap.
issues.solution: Track masks_purchased as the number of successful purchases per day (attempted minus unmet). Define stockout_events as days or retailers where stock reaches zero (independent of purchase attempts). Implement subgroup_adoption_gap (e.g., income quintile top minus bottom, or as per chosen subgroup definition) and report it.

issues.description: Stockout flag only set when a purchase is attempted and stock is zero, missing days where stock is zero but no attempts occur.
issues.solution: Set retailer_stockout_today if supply.available_mask_stock == 0 at any time during the day, not only when a purchase is attempted. Optionally track stockout duration across the day.

issues.description: Watts–Strogatz initialization yields degree k-1 for odd requested degrees due to half_k = k // 2 (neighbors added on one side only).
issues.solution: Ensure exact average degree k by adding neighbors symmetrically or adjusting construction to handle odd k (e.g., randomly adding an extra neighbor for half the nodes).

issues.description: Subgroup adoption metrics diverge from spec (Gini and SES disparity computed instead of the specified subgroup_adoption_gap metric).
issues.solution: Explicitly compute subgroup_adoption_gap per the chosen subgroup definition (e.g., difference between top and bottom income quintiles) and expose it under the correct metric name.

issues.description: With population_size up to 10,000, the O(N*k) network construction and per-step O(N+E) loops are acceptable, but the code may become slow for larger N or long horizons.
issues.solution: If needed, optimize neighbor influence computations (precompute degrees, vectorize with NumPy) and avoid repeated Python-level loops. Current performance is likely acceptable for N≈10k and 120 days.

issues.description: The CLI --steps handling ignores parameters.simulation_duration_days in the input structure and only reads top-level keys.
issues.solution: When steps is not provided, check data['parameters'].get('simulation_duration_days') before defaulting to 30.

issues.description: The SocialNetwork behavior and media targeting strategies from the spec are placeholders or absent.
issues.location: Classes MediaOutlet, SimulationEnvironment (no SocialNetwork class), and related usage
issues.solution: Implement SocialNetwork with propagate_social_influence and rewiring per parameters; implement media targeting and trust modifiers per channels.
